page1.text:
Her lungs are on fire.
Her heart's been drumming a warning signal for some time from within the confines of her chest.
Ba-dump, ba-dump, squeeze, ba-dump.
It cries out in protest as it vomits blood through her body, like an old man groaning that he's on his last legs.

page3.text:
Her throat is in pain.
Each breath feels like swallowing thorns.
It's so terrifying, she can't breathe.
She's low on oxygen, but she suicidally stops herself from breathing.

page5.text:
Without oxygen, her arms and legs can't move very well.
She's made it this far on unsteady legs, but she could collapse at any time.

page7.text:
The thought gives her a burst of strength.
She can't let herself fall here.
It would defeat the whole point of sneaking out.
She—I'm going to settle my own unfinished business right here, right now.
She can't stop, even if she and the old man who turned her into a Master end up killing each other.

page9.text:
...She gets her breath under control.
It's going to be all right. This won't be that hard.
It might be for anyone else, but not for her.
She just needs to look the old man in the face like she does when they're eating together, shake her head, and say "no."
Then...then his schemes will come to an end.

page10.text:
...She doesn't consider what will happen to her after she denies the fiend's will.
If she does, she won't be able to go through with it.
So she doesn't think too hard about it.
Fortunately, her memories are becoming less clear by the second.
The fear isn't so bad, since she won't even remember what's going to happen next.

page11.text:
It's been several days since she was back in her house.
She walks through the dark rooms, using the walls for support.
She searches her scattered memory, but she can't remember a time when this house was ever bright.
The house is the same as usual.
It's wicked, corrupt, and sticky like it always is.
But...

page12.text:
"No... Why?"
This isn't what she expected.
Her grandfather isn't here.
She can't sense any of the bugs in the building.

page13.text:
"...Hah... Ah, aahh..."
She looks through the empty rooms, trying to support her failing body.
This is strange.
This is strange.
This is strange.
The old man isn't in the Matou mansion.
His laughing voice isn't in the basement.

page14.text:
"No... Why..."
It doesn't make sense.
Zouken Matou—Grandfather wants to take me back.
I thought that he wouldn't make a move as long as I was at the Emiya house.
So now is his best chance.
If I'm alone, he should show up and try to turn me into a Holy Grail.
So...where is he?

page15.text:
"Ah... haah... haah... ah..."
...Her consciousness grows faint.
...That won't do.
She needs to find Zouken Matou before she falls asleep. Before Shirou Emiya acts.
She needs to find him and end this.
It would all be over if she met him, so why... Why isn't he here today of all days!?

page16.text:
"I know...but...!"
Of course he's aware.
He's always watching me. No matter how far I am or where I hide, he'll always find me.
He could easily capture me right now and make me do what he wants.
He won't care whether I want to or not.
He's always treated me as nothing but a tool.

page17.text:
"But...why..."
There's no way he's unaware.
It doesn't matter that the priest reduced the number of worms in my body.
...They were just insurance.
That old man has other ways of tracking me.
Of knowing my physical condition. He's even listening to my heartbeat.
He knows that I left Rider and came here alone.
After all, he's always—
